name: Adelaide
title: Adelaide Ship Thickness Measurement | Grain & Car Carrier UTM
description: Thickness gauging at Port Adelaide and Outer Harbor for grain bulk carriers, car carriers, container ships and tankers: holds, ballast tanks, decks, piping.
h1: Ultrasonic Gauging for Ships at Port Adelaide and Outer Harbor
intro: Adelaide's port complex lies along the Port River and Gulf St Vincent and is run by Flinders Ports. Outer Harbor, at the river mouth, handles container ships, grain carriers, car carriers, fuel tankers and cruise ships; the Inner Harbour at Port Adelaide takes smaller bulk and cargo ships. Grain carriers loading after the South Australian harvest are the main gauging prospects, and lay-up berths add time for wider scopes. With no commercial dry dock for deep-sea ships, our technicians travel from India and work alongside or at anchor.

highlights.h: Holds ready for the grain inspection
highlights.p: Before loading export grain, a ship's holds must pass an inspection by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry. Clean, empty holds are also the easiest to gauge, so hold frames, hopper plating and hatch coamings can be measured in the same window.

highlights.h: Lay-up berths with time for a full scope
highlights.p: Flinders Ports lists lay-up use at Outer Harbor Berth 1 and Inner Harbour Berth 25. A ship waiting there for employment or a sale has no cargo deadline, which allows a thorough condition survey across its tanks, holds and decks.

highlights.h: Fast calls by car and container ships
highlights.p: Car carriers and container ships at Outer Harbor work to tight schedules. Gauging on these calls concentrates on weather decks, ramps, coamings, lashing structure and scrubber piping, measured while cargo operations continue around the team.

port.h: Port Adelaide and Outer Harbor on Gulf St Vincent
p: The Port River runs north through Adelaide's north-western suburbs to Gulf St Vincent, with the Lefevre Peninsula separating it from the open gulf. The historic Inner Harbour at Port Adelaide sits upriver and is limited to smaller ships, while Outer Harbor, near the river mouth, takes larger vessels with deeper water and wider swing basins. Ships approach through Gulf St Vincent, which Kangaroo Island and the Fleurieu and Yorke peninsulas shelter from the Southern Ocean swell, and those waiting for a berth anchor in the gulf off Outer Harbor. Winter brings cold fronts and strong south-westerly winds that can hold up launch transfers and berthing, while summer is generally settled. Flinders Ports, which runs the complex, also operates regional ports elsewhere in South Australia, several of them busy in the grain season.

Outer Harbor carries most of the deep-sea traffic. The Flinders Adelaide Container Terminal occupies berths 6 and 7, and Berth 8 is a dedicated grain loading wharf, while other berths handle motor vehicles, the passenger terminal and a common-user fuel berth for medium and long range product tankers. Upriver, the Inner Harbour berths handle fertilisers, steel, cement, limestone, grain and petroleum products, and bunkers are supplied at the inner berths from a fuel terminal at Largs North. Grain dominates the bulk calendar. South Australia's harvest begins late in the year, and grain carriers then load through the summer and autumn at Outer Harbor and at the regional ports, sometimes completing their cargo at a second port in the gulfs. Cruise ships visit through the southern summer, and car carriers and container ships call all year.

Ship repair in Adelaide is mainly a small-craft business. The Osborne precinct on the Lefevre Peninsula is a naval shipbuilding site rather than a commercial repair yard, and there is no dry dock that merchant ships trading here would use; deep-sea vessels dock in Asian yards when their surveys fall due. That makes Adelaide gauging a matter of berth and anchorage work, timed to the ship's cargo or lay-up. It also gives the port a useful role in an owner's planning: a grain carrier loading for Asia, or a car carrier on a liner rotation through Australia, can have its critical spaces gauged here and the readings sent to the yard well before the ship arrives. For ships laid up at Port Adelaide, a full condition survey can be carried out with no cargo pressure at all.

facilities.h: Grain, container, vehicle and lay-up berths
p: Each kind of berth gives a different window. At the grain wharf, holds are cleaned and inspected before loading, and the period between the hold inspection and the first cargo is the best time to gauge hold structure; ballast tanks become available as the ship deballasts. Container ships and car carriers at Outer Harbor offer short calls, so the work is limited to deck structure, hatch coamings, ramps, lashing bridges, accessible tanks and the scrubber discharge line. Product tankers at the fuel berth allow deck and piping readings under the terminal's rules. The lay-up berths are the most generous of all: a ship waiting there can open every tank and hold in turn for a complete survey.

Ships at anchor in Gulf St Vincent can be reached by launch, booked by the agent, though winter weather sometimes stops transfers. Inner Harbour ships are smaller and their stays tend to be longer, which suits condition gauging on general cargo and bulk ships carrying cement, limestone or fertiliser. Small local craft such as tugs, ferries and fishing boats are serviced on small slipways along the Port River, and they can be gauged when they come out of the water. For anything larger, the nearest suitable docking is in Asia, so readings taken in Adelaide are planned as a pre-docking estimate.
list: Outer Harbor Berth 8 grain wharf: hold, hopper and topside tank gauging on bulk carriers between the hold inspection and loading
Flinders Adelaide Container Terminal (berths 6 and 7): coaming, deck and scrubber pipe readings during working calls
Outer Harbor vehicle and passenger berths: weather deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging on car carriers
Outer Harbor 4 fuel berth: deck and pipe wall-thickness checks on product tankers under terminal permits
Lay-up berths (Outer Harbor 1 and Inner Harbour 25): full condition surveys with no cargo deadline
Gulf St Vincent anchorage: owner's condition and pre-purchase gauging by launch

context.h: Port state control, grain hold inspections and biosecurity
p: AMSA carries out port state control in South Australia as part of its national programme under the Tokyo MoU and the Indian Ocean MoU. Grain carriers face a second gate: before loading export grain, their holds are inspected by officers of the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, and a ship whose holds carry loose rust scale, flaking coatings, cargo residues or insects can fail and be sent away to clean. Corroded frames and peeling paint are a frequent cause of trouble, because scale traps residues and pests. Owners who know the condition of their hold steel can plan repairs and coating work before the season, and the thickness record helps them decide whether a hold needs renewal or only cleaning and touch-up.

Biosecurity runs through the whole arrival process. International ships report their biofouling management to the department through the Maritime Arrivals Reporting System before reaching Australian waters, and ballast water discharged in the gulf must meet Australia's management requirements. Car carriers and other ships arriving from certain countries also face heightened measures during the brown marmorated stink bug season, which runs from September to April and affects how cargo and ships are treated on arrival. None of these rules concern steel thickness directly, but they shape the timing of a call and the inspections a ship goes through, and an inspection plan that fits around them saves the ship time in port.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs at Port Adelaide and Outer Harbor
jobs.p: Adelaide jobs follow the grain calendar and the lay-up market. In the export season, owners and charterers ask for hold and ballast tank gauging on bulk carriers before loading, either to plan repairs or to support a pre-docking estimate for an Asian yard. Ships in lay-up at Outer Harbor or the Inner Harbour attract condition surveys and pre-purchase inspections, because buyers can see every space without cargo in the way. Car carriers and container ships produce shorter jobs on deck structure and scrubber piping. We confirm the scope with the superintendent, line up access through the agent and Flinders Ports, and travel from India once the berth or lay-up dates are fixed; reports follow the class TM formats.
list: Hold frame, hopper plating and hatch coaming gauging on a Panamax bulk carrier at Outer Harbor Berth 8 before grain loading
Pre-purchase gauging of a bulk carrier in lay-up at Inner Harbour Berth 25, covering every tank and hold
Pre-docking steel estimate on a car carrier on its Australian rotation, focused on the weather deck, ramps and ballast tanks
Scrubber wash-water and overboard pipe gauging on a container ship at the Flinders Adelaide Container Terminal
Condition gauging of a cement carrier's tanks and deck during an Inner Harbour discharge

logistics: The team flies into Adelaide Airport, usually through an Asian hub or another Australian city, and reaches Outer Harbor or Port Adelaide by road. An Australian visa covering short-term specialist work is obtained before departure, so its lead time is part of the plan from the first enquiry. The ship's agent arranges berth and terminal access with Flinders Ports, and visiting technicians work under escort in the port's security zones. Launches to the gulf anchorage are booked through the agent.

faqs.q: Can a grain carrier be gauged before the department's hold inspection?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is a sensible order of work. Gauging before the inspection shows whether rust scale or wasted steel is likely to cause trouble, and leaves time for cleaning or repair. Gauging after a passed inspection is also possible, but the team must leave the holds as clean as they found them, so we agree the timing with the master and the loading agent.

faqs.q: Is a ship laid up at Port Adelaide a good candidate for a full condition survey?
faqs.a: It is one of the best. With no cargo operations and no departure deadline, every tank, hold and void can be opened, ventilated and gauged in a planned sequence, and the crew has time to provide lighting and access. Buyers and owners use these surveys before a sale, a reactivation or a docking, and the report gives them a complete picture rather than a sample.

faqs.q: Is there a dry dock in Adelaide for merchant ships?
faqs.a: No. The Osborne precinct builds naval ships, and the local slipways serve small craft. Bulk carriers, car carriers and container ships trading to Adelaide dock in Asian yards. The useful Adelaide service for those ships is a pre-docking estimate, gauging the spaces most likely to need steel during a cargo call or lay-up, so the owner can agree the renewal scope before the docking.

faqs.q: Can the team follow a grain ship to its second loading port?
faqs.a: Yes, if the timing works. Grain carriers sometimes load part of their cargo at Outer Harbor and complete at another South Australian port, and the scope can be split between the two calls. The agent confirms access at each port, and we plan travel by road or domestic flight so the team reaches the second port before the ship arrives.

faqs.q: Can car carriers be gauged during an Outer Harbor call?
faqs.a: Within limits. Car carrier calls are short and vehicle decks are busy during discharge, so the scope usually covers the weather deck, ramps, hoistable deck supports where accessible, ballast tanks and the scrubber discharge line. A larger survey of the internal decks is better planned for a lay-up period or a docking, when the decks are empty and access is easier.
